Inverse rotations preserve size, and a non-growing initial inverse b can be deleted by monotonicity without losing eventual growth. Therefore a shortest extending word must be ba^j for the first cyclic 0-to-1 boundary. Prefix count 1^k0^(j+1-k) gives (j+1)2^(n-j-2) subsets at j<n-1 and n-1 endpoint subsets at j=n-1; sum/mean/limit verified symbolically. Independent reverse-subset BFS through n=10 reproduced each individual length and the full histogram; uniqueness also follows from deletion plus the first-boundary rule. The claim concerns first size increase, not reset rank.
